item.title: TechWolf acquired in largest Belgian VC-backed software deal
item.description:
TechWolf acquired in largest Belgian VC-backed software deal

TechWolf, a Belgian AI company that provides workforce skills-mapping software, has been acquired in what its co-founder describes as the largest acquisition of a venture-capital-backed software company in Belgian history. No financial details have been disclosed.

🔍 Overview

Founded in 2018 by Ghent University students Andreas De Neve, Jeroen van Hautte and Mikaël Wornoo, TechWolf develops AI software that gives companies an overview of their employees’ skills by drawing on data from business systems. The company is headquartered in Ghent, with additional offices in London and New York, and is opening a San Francisco office this year.

💰 Funding History

  • In 2020, the Flemish government’s investment company PMV invested in TechWolf.
  • Further funding rounds followed in 2022 and 2024, raising €10 million and €40 million respectively.
  • SAP was an investor in the 2024 round.
  • PMV also participated in both the 2022 and 2024 funding rounds. It is unclear how large a stake PMV holds in TechWolf.

📊 Recent Financials

In its most recent financial year, ending in January 2026, TechWolf reported revenue of €8.68 million.

Source: SAP acquires Ghent-based AI company TechWolf

item.title: AMD to Acquire World Labs in $8.2 Billion All-Stock Deal
item.description:
AMD to Acquire World Labs in $8.2 Billion All-Stock Deal

AMD has announced an all-stock acquisition of World Labs, an AI research lab co-founded by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, for approximately $8.2 billion.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deal Value: Approximately $8.2 billion
  • Deal Structure: All-stock
  • Expected Closing: By the end of the year

🔍 Overview

World Labs launched in 2024 and reached a valuation of $1 billion within a few months. The company developed the following product:

Product Function
Marble A world generation model that allows users to create interactive 3D worlds from a prompt

💡 Why it matters

AMD stated the acquisition will strengthen its “ability to develop AI hardware, software and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications.”

Following the acquisition:

  • Dr. Fei-Fei Li will become EVP and chief scientist at AMD, reporting to CEO Lisa Su.
  • The World Labs team will “continue to focus on advancing AI model research.”

This acquisition follows other significant AI deals, including Nvidia’s announcement earlier this month that it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion.

#AMD #WorldLabs #AIResearch #Acquisition

Source: AMD is acquiring AI company World Labs in a deal worth more than $8 billion

item.title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
item.description:
Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion

Nvidia has agreed to purchase Hugging Face, the popular open-source AI platform, for $12.93 billion.

🔍 Overview

  • Hugging Face is an online platform founded in 2016 that hosts open-source AI models, datasets, and tools.
  • It is often described as the “GitHub” for AI due to its browsable library and community collaboration features.

⚙️ Key details

  • The acquisition price is $12.93 billion, nearly triple Hugging Face’s last valuation of $4.5 billion in 2023.
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated: “Together, we will scale Hugging Face’s platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide.”
  • Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem.
  • Developers will retain the choice of models, frameworks, clouds, inference service providers, and computing platforms.
  • Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

📅 Timeline

  • Speculation began on August 23rd after reports that Hugging Face was exploring a $13 billion sale.
  • By August 27th, reports indicated Nvidia was in acquisition talks with Hugging Face, with earlier claims of a $12.9 billion deal already agreed upon.
  • Nvidia has now publicly declared its intent to purchase Hugging Face.

💡 Why it matters

  • Nvidia gains a strategic foothold to help preserve its AI hardware dominance as closed-source AI providers develop their own chips.
  • Hugging Face previously rejected a $500 million investment offer from Nvidia in 2023, which would have valued it at $7 billion.
  • Hugging Face generates around $150 million in annualized revenue, a fraction of its purchase price.

#Nvidia #HuggingFace #AI #acquisition #open-source #AIhardware

Source: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for almost $13 billion
